{"qas": [
  {"question": "According to arXiv 2510.03368, how does the ARGO Framework address both inconsistent RAI implementation and accountability challenges?", "answer": "The ARGO Framework uses three layers: a shared foundation for minimum standards and role clarity, and a local implementation layer for contextual adaptation and explicit accountability.", "evidence": [{"page": 7, "quote": "The ARGO Framework recognizes that AI development, deployment, and use occur across multiple organizational levels (Fig. 2). It defines three interdependent layers that work together to support consistent and contextually appropriate RAI practices."}, {"page": 7, "quote": "By explicitly designating local responsibilities, it addresses the accountability challenges observed in our assessment."}]},
  {"question": "What two main types of data sources were used for the RAI assessment in arXiv 2510.03368?", "answer": "The assessment used written responses/interviews and document review as primary data sources.", "evidence": [{"page": 5, "quote": "Three primary data sources informed the assessment:

Written responses and interviews. The assessment began with semi-structured interviews, preceded by the distribution of question sets (see example questions in Appendix A) to key stakeholders."}, {"page": 5, "quote": "Document review. Supporting documentation, including AI development and deployment workflows, internal governance materials, and project-level documentation, was reviewed to cross-check reported practices and identify potential gaps."}]},
  {"question": "In arXiv 2510.03368, what does the ARGO Framework's 'Advisory and Tooling Layer' provide to business units?", "answer": "It provides RAI toolkits, training, technical assets, reporting mechanisms, centralized AI assets, validation, standardized templates, and feedback channels.", "evidence": [{"page": 7, "quote": "At this level, centralized group-level teams provide:

· RAI toolkits (e.g., fairness metrics libraries, explainability dashboards)

· Training programs and playbooks

· Technical assets integrated into core development platforms

· Lightweight reporting mechanisms to improve visibility across units

· Centralization of common AI assets at the group level with applied RAI practices to serve as implementation models

· Validation of guidelines through application to grouplevel AI assets

· Standardized templates and documentation guidelines for consistent implementation across business units

· Feedback channels for business units to report if any group-level assets are not working for their specific use case - or if they do particularly well."}]},
  {"question": "According to arXiv 2510.03368, what does 'RAI' stand for?", "answer": "RAI stands for Responsible AI.", "evidence": [{"page": 5, "quote": "The evaluation framework covered nine dimensions of RAI, selected to align with major industry and regulatory frameworks based on the dimensions outlined in (Reuel et al. 2024), while also reflecting internal governance discussions."}]},
  {"question": "Which governance approach in arXiv 2510.03368 supports both minimum standards and local adaptation, and how is this described in the comparison table?", "answer": "The ARGO Framework supports layered authority with shared minimum standards and local contextualization.", "evidence": [{"page": 8, "quote": "| Decision Authority           | Concentrated in central ethics boards or committees     | Dispersed across autonomous units with limited coordination | Layered authority with shared minimum standards and local contextualization    |"}]},
  {"question": "In arXiv 2510.03368, how are informal feedback loops described as contributing to RAI governance?", "answer": "Informal feedback loops, such as sharing post-deployment model behavior, support internal learning and normalization of responsible review.", "evidence": [{"page": 10, "quote": "Several teams implement informal feedback loops, such as sharing unexpected post-deployment model behavior or reflecting on incidents. While these mechanisms are often ad hoc, they support internal learning and normalization of ethical and responsible review."}]}
]}
